description: Same great education, exciting new location for 2026 - Join us this fall in one of San Francisco's most distinctive neighborhoods at the beautifully reimagined Hotel Kabuki! Join us for an engaging and practical OBGYN CME conference designed to keep clinicians at the forefront of Reproductive healthcare. This program will highlight the latest evidence and clinical updates across a range of important topics, including complex contraception, gynecologic surgery, cancer prevention, and menopausal care. Expert faculty will share insights on managing both common and complex conditions in obstetrics and gynecology, with a focus on translating new data into everyday clinical practice. Through concise, evidence-based lectures, participants will gain practical strategies for improving patient care across the reproductive lifespan. Attendees will leave with actionable tools to enhance surgical decision-making, strengthen patient counseling, and implement clinical protocols that improve outcomes for diverse patient populations. Whether you are looking to refine your approach to chronic conditions in pregnancy, stay current on updates in reproductive health, or incorporate new guidelines into practice, this conference will provide the knowledge and confidence to elevate your everyday care. Onsite and Remote Learning Options: The course will be offered as a live conference. Registrants have the option to attend in person or to tune in remotely via zoom live stream during programming hours (Pacific Time). Login instructions along with the digital syllabus will be shared with attendees before the meeting. Included in your registration fee is access to the course recordings on demand after the conference and for 30 days after the course. You must tune in to the live conference (in person or remotely) to claim CME. Registration Fees - Early Bird Pricing in effect until 9/5/2026: Physicians: $825 / $875Nurses/APPs/Other Health Care Professionals: $675 / $725Residents/Trainees/Fellows: $525 / $575For more information and to register, please visit: https://ucsf.cloud-cme.com/obgyn2026

description: In honor of National Caregiver Month, the UCSF Neuro-Oncology Gordon Murray Caregiver Program invites you to join a panel conversation with three caregivers. Caregiving looks different for everyone, but at its heart, the experience is universal. Join us for an honest, moving conversation with three caregivers sharing their unique journeys: Michelle Mathai, who cared for her brother; Mark Kunerth, who cared for his wife while raising their daughter; and Jesse Brisendine, who is currently caring for his longtime partner. Through Q&As, our panelists will share the challenges, lessons, and unexpected moments of grace that come with caregiving. From the early days of stepping into the role to the realities of caring for a loved one over time, our panelists hope to inspire reflection and insights that many caregivers can resonate with. description: We are delighted to welcome you to the 2nd International Conference on Neuropsychiatry, scheduled for November 06-07, 2026, in Dubai, UAE. This prestigious event will bring together leading experts, researchers, and clinicians in the field of neuropsychiatry to explore the intricate connection between the brain and mind. Theme: Exploring the Frontiers of Brain Science and Mental Health in Neuropsychiatry Neuropsychiatry 2026 promises to be an inspiring forum for discussing ground breaking research, therapies, and treatment modalities aimed at understanding and addressing brain-related psychiatric disorders. With a focus on the intersection of neuroscience and psychiatry, the conference will delve into emerging approaches to managing mental health conditions and neurological diseases, offering a platform for meaningful discussions, presentations, and networking opportunities. This conference will provide invaluable insights into the latest advances in neuropsychiatric treatment, offering healthcare professionals, researchers, and policymakers a chance to deepen their knowledge, discover innovative therapies, and explore new possibilities in the field. Through expert-led seminars and cutting-edge sessions, participants will engage with emerging trends and treatment strategies for conditions such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression, neurodegenerative diseases, and more. The Neuropsychiatry 2026 conference will feature scientific sessions focusing on the most relevant and advanced topics in the field, including the neurobiological underpinnings of psychiatric disorders, cutting-edge treatment methodologies, and the application of artificial intelligence and neuroimaging in diagnosis and therapy. This will be a unique opportunity to engage with the latest research, clinical practices, and innovations shaping the future of neuropsychiatry. For those unable to attend in person, we are pleased to offer virtual participation. Join us online to attend live sessions, engage in real-time Q&As, and access exclusive resources from the comfort of your own location. This hybrid format ensures that participants can benefit from the conference regardless of geographical constraints, offering a flexible and accessible way to stay up-to-date with the field’s advancements. Don’t miss the chance to be part of this ground breaking event in one of the world’s most iconic cities—Dubai, UAE. We look forward to welcoming you to Neuropsychiatry 2026, where the future of brain-mind research and treatment will be unveiled.

description: Join us for our Stem Cell Genome Engineering Series | Organoid Models, which highlights advances in genome engineering for stem cell biology and therapeutic development, aligning with our vision to Discover, Engineer, Heal. At our Nov 10 session, we will hear from speaker Michelle Gbenedio, who will present "Patient-Derived Organoid Resources: From 3D Model Development to Disease Modeling and Drug Screening." Advances in organoid technology have offered new opportunities for studying human biology and disease in vitro. In collaboration with UCSF clinicians, the Organoid Core has established a living organoid biobank of over 100 organoid lines to serve as a platform for collaborative research at UCSF. The talk will cover how these 3D models are generated and used for downstream applications like genomic and biomarker analyses as well as testing therapeutic responses. Speaker Lineup | Fall 2026 Oct 13 | Dan Wagner | Single-Cell Genomics: From Cell Atlases to Genotype-Resolved Biology Oct 27 | James Gardner | Normothermic perfusion systems as platforms for groundbreaking ex vivo human biology Nov 10 | Michelle Gbenedio | Getting started with organoids Dec 8 | Alex Pollen | Experimental and analytical techniques for village culture organoids UCSF welcomes all participants to our events. description: Making Health Promotion Meaningful: Community-engaged Strategies for Reaching Diverse Priority Populations Presented by Simona C. Kwon, DrPH, MPH Simona C. Kwon, DrPH, MPH, is an associate professor in the Department of Population Health at NYU Grossman School of Medicine and serves as director of the NYU Center for the Study of Asian American Health. She is nationally recognized for her expertise in community-based participatory research (CBPR) and health equity initiatives aimed at reducing health disparities in immigrant and minority populations. Dr. Kwon’s research focuses on chronic disease prevention, cultural competency in healthcare, and the social determinants of health. She has led multiple NIH-funded projects addressing health issues in underserved communities, with a particular focus on Asian American populations. As a leader in public health, Dr. Kwon collaborates with community-based organizations to design and implement culturally tailored interventions. Her work highlights the importance of building trust and partnerships between healthcare systems and the communities they serve. She has published extensively on CBPR methodologies and health equity frameworks. Dr. Kwon is committed to advancing inclusive and equitable approaches to improving health outcomes across diverse populations. Learning Objectives: At the end of this activity, learners will be able to: Apply key principles of social marketing and cultural adaptation that can inform efforts to close gaps between current and ideal practice in health promotion and disease prevention for reaching priority populations. Describe how community engagement, participatory approaches, and cultural relevance can support more whole-person, integrated care through clinical practice, research, and education for diverse priority populations. Identify broad strategies for adapting evidence-based health programs to improve relevance, implementation, and sustainability in priority communities, with the goal of improving health outcomes. Accreditation Statement Continuing Education: This UCSF continuing education activity was planned and developed to: uphold academic standards to ensure balance, independence, objectivity, and scientific rigor; adhere to requirements to protect health information under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA); and, include a mechanism to inform learners when unapproved or unlabeled uses of therapeutic products or agents are discussed or referenced. UCSF adheres to the ACCME’s Standards for Integrity and Independence in Accredited Continuing Education. Any individuals in a position to control the content of a CE activity, including content planners, reviewers, authors, presenters, moderators, panelists, or others are required to disclose all financial relationships with ineligible entities. All relevant financial relationships have been mitigated prior to the commencement of the activity. Accreditation: In support of improving patient care, the University of California, San Francisco Office of Continuing Medical Education (CME) is jointly accredited by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), to provide continuing education for the healthcare team. This CME activity meets the requirements under California Assembly 1195, continuing education, and cultural and linguistic competency. UCSF designates this live activity for a maximum of 10 AMA PRA Category 1 credit(s)TM. Attendees should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. The credit maximum above reflects all Osher Center for Integrative Health Grand Rounds sessions in Fiscal Year 2027. Up to 1 credit may be claimed against any individual session. In order to receive credit you must certify your attendance in this session and claim your credits earned in the activity within 6 days of its conclusion.
